name: Canada
sources: GDP $596bn current US$ and population 27.7m (World Bank national accounts, 1990).

Inflation 4.8%: Statistics Canada CPI, annual average 1990. Interest rate 0.13 is the Bank of Canada bank rate, which averaged about 13% over 1990 and peaked at 14.05% in May; John Crow's zero-inflation target and the defence of the dollar kept it far above the US rate.
Tax 42% of GDP is total general-government revenue (federal, provincial, municipal, CPP/QPP) on the OECD basis; the GST was legislated in 1990 and took effect 1 January 1991.

Defence 2.0% of GDP: NATO and NORAD member with a mechanised brigade group and air division in Germany. Strength 12 reflects 87,000 regulars, no strategic reach and no nuclear weapons - a large NATO contributor, not a power.
Debt 73% of GDP is general-government gross financial liabilities (OECD, 1990); federal net debt alone was about 55%.
Oil 1.55 mbd is 1990 crude oil production; Canadian totals including NGLs and synthetic crude run near 2.0 mbd (BP Statistical Review).

Separatism 0.35: the Meech Lake Accord died on 23 June 1990, the Bloc Quebecois was founded that summer, Quebec sovereignty polling passed 60%, and the Oka standoff ran July-September. Stability 66 records a constitutional crisis inside an otherwise settled democracy.
Investment shares: gross fixed capital formation was about 21.5% of GDP in 1990, split roughly 3% public and 18.5% private (Statistics Canada).
